subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex Action 1.11's GitHub-hosted Linux setup that enables unprivileged user namespaces and clears the AppArmor userns restriction in the four agent workflows?
rationale: The upstream change intentionally alters host-level sandbox prerequisites before secret-bearing agent execution, so repository automation cannot decide whether that tradeoff matches OpenClaw's CI security policy. ([github.com](https://github.com/openai/codex-action/blob/52fe01ec70a42f454c9d2ebd47598f9fd6893d56/action.yml))

options.title: Split the Codex bump
options.body: Merge the routine action updates separately and review Codex Action 1.11 with focused workflow and security evidence.

options.title: Accept the grouped update
options.body: Approve the host-policy change after representative docs-agent, Mantis, maturity, and test-performance workflow runs complete successfully.

options.title: Retain the current Codex pin
options.body: Keep Codex Action 1.8 until an alternative avoids globally relaxing the AppArmor userns restriction.

recommendation.title: Split the Codex bump
recommendation.body: Merge the routine action updates separately and review Codex Action 1.11 with focused workflow and security evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership signal across both Codex-backed agent workflows and CI action-runtime policy.
